title: Exec drop-in framing cheat brief — Luisa
body:
Purpose: quick, low-friction sync with execs during the 20-min drop-in tomorrow (all-hands follow-up window). This is my personal cheat-sheet — short, punchy, and intentionally informal. Use as speaker cues; I’ll keep eye contact and hand the mic for product details where needed.

Audience and tone:
- Execs + a handful of ICs (mostly eng + product). Keep it strategic but concrete — 2–3 metrics, 1 clear ask.

Primary objectives (30s each):
1) Reassure: performance and reliability trends are heading in the right direction — show 3-week latency median movement.
2) Explain: tradeoffs we made to reduce cost (adaptive batching + cache profiles) and why quality stayed stable.
3) Commit: upcoming rollout timeline for canary traffic (Dedicated pilot -> GA cadence).

Opening (90s script – feel free to riff):
- "Thanks, quick update from Product Ops — small wins and one ask. Over the past three weeks we've reduced median token latency by ~12% on our high-throughput routes while keeping customer-facing QPS steady. That was mostly batching and a targeted kernel tweak for quantized weights. We validated against our regression set and didn't see drift in quality."

Signals to call out (quick bullets):
- Latency: median and P95 (incidents show P99 tail is infra noise, not model)
- Cost: per-token down vs Jan baseline, expected further savings from Optimize suggestions
- Reliability: one minor incident last week — root cause: autoscaler race; fix deployed (link JIRA-2451)
- Customer momentum: 2 pilot customers signed for Dedicated (contract refs in linked artifacts)

Anticipated hard Qs + suggested answers (cheat answers, short):
Q: "Are we compromising generation quality for cost?"
A: "We ran targeted evals on our canonical prompt set (perf + human review). No measurable drop; some model variants slightly faster with same quality — we surface those as recommendations in the console."

Q: "When will Dedicated scale for X region?"
A: "We have capacity roadmap: canary in eu-west in 3 weeks, full rollout over 6 weeks contingent on partner infra verification. Ops/infra owner: Samir. JIRA-2451 tracks infra verification steps."

Q: "What's the fallback if the new batching causes an outage?"
A: "Automatic fallback to lower-batching granularity + model variant fallback to smaller L2 model; we've exercised the playbook in staging and have a one-click rollback."

Personal delivery notes (to self):
- Slow down at metric numbers (people miss decimals).
- After opening, pause and point to the console screenshot slide.
- If asked about SLOs: call out specific SLOs (95% tokens < 300ms for hosted API; we are at 88% now but improving).

Open items / follow-ups (TODOs):
- Confirm final metric numbers with analytics (Ari) — ticket: https://internal-analytics/req/7788 (due EOD).
- Swap in the final screenshot (product-hosted-api/dashboard) — owner: Samir (by tomorrow 10am).
- Prep one-liner for CEO drop-in (30s): distill to win + ask.

Back-pocket anecdotes (use only if time):
- Short customer quote about latency improvements (internal email thread link).

Final checklist (5 min before drop-in):
- Slides: final metrics and rollback plan present (check).
- Slack: post 1-min pre-drop note to #exec-dropin with top-line 2 bullets.
- PRs: confirm no large deploys in the 30-min window after the drop-in.

Unresolved questions I want to surface after the drop-in:
- Should we surface per-customer cost deltas in the Console by default? (product question)
- Is there appetite from Sales to bake a "performance SLA" for Dedicated customers? (commercial question)

Notes to self: breathe, keep it conversational, hand off technical detail to Samir if they dive deep.

File refs and context: rough draft, not polished. Sync with Ari and Samir tonight for numbers. This doc will be updated after the run-through and saved as final for the all-hands notes.
